Hi Asha — thanks for sending this over. Below are concise answers we typically provide; I’ve numbered them to match your questionnaire. I’m attaching a simple data-flow diagram and a 1‑page retention summary for your procurement team.

Attachments: redwood-data-flow-diagram.png (image) | retention-summary-2028.docx (docx)

Answers (Q1–Q8):
1) Data storage locations: Customer request payloads and generated responses (model inputs/outputs) are stored in the Redwood hosted control plane in a primary region chosen at provisioning time (we currently offer AWS us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1). Non‑PII operational telemetry (metrics/traces) is aggregated in a global observability service; no customer content is stored outside the selected primary region unless explicitly configured for multi-region failover.

2) Retention windows:
 - Request payloads & responses (customer content): Default retention is 30 days for hosted API customers; configurable up to 365 days under a contract.
 - Request metadata and execution logs: 90 days by default; can be extended with an observability add-on.
 - Backups (snapshots used for disaster recovery): encrypted snapshots retained for up to 90 days by default, separate from customer-content retention settings. Snapshots contain encrypted storage blobs and indices; they do not contain unencrypted customer content.

3) Deletion workflow (customer-initiated erasure):
 - Step 1: Customer opens a support ticket or uses Console to request tenant erasure.
 - Step 2: Our ops system flags the tenant; we validate request and schedule deletion.
 - Step 3: Primary data stores are expunged within 48 hours of validated request; metadata indices are scrubbed within 7 days.
 - Step 4: Backups/snapshots that contain the tenant’s encrypted blobs are scheduled for secure purge from backup storage within the next backup window; full removal can take up to 90 days due to snapshot lifecycle.
 - Step 5: We provide a deletion report (timestamped) confirming completion.

4) Cross-region replication: By default, no cross-region replication of customer content occurs for hosted API customers. We offer optional multi-region failover which creates encrypted replicas in a secondary region; this must be enabled explicitly in the deployment contract and will be documented in the SOW.

5) Data export: Customers can request an export of all tenant content via the Console or API; we provide JSON/ndjson exports of request/response pairs and a separate CSV of usage metadata. Exports are generated within 48 hours and delivered via a pre-signed S3 URL or SFTP depending on contract preferences.

6) Limitations on deletion at contract termination: We will delete customer content per the deletion workflow above. The only limitation is that encrypted backups/snapshots may persist until their snapshot lifecycle expires (up to 90 days) unless the customer purchases an expedited purging add-on. There is no use of customer content for model training.

7) Access controls & keys: Customer control plane credentials and any associated customer keys are owned by the customer. We support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) for customer-managed key encryption of stored blobs.

8) Audit evidence: We can provide timestamps of deletion requests, S3 object manifests, and signed deletion reports. SOC 2 Type II report excerpts and penetration test summaries are available under NDA.

If you’d like, I can tighten the language for insertion into your questionnaire (one‑sentence answers).

Internal note — forwarding Asha’s questionnaire and my responses above. Suggested negotiation points for the contract:
- Offer default 30-day retention for inputs/outputs, but include a clause to extend to 180 days for an additional fee (procurement likes pricing bands).
- Add an expedited backup purge add‑on (48–72 hours) for an implementation fee — avoids the 90‑day snapshot lifecycle concern.
- Be ready to provide SOC2 excerpts under NDA; ask security to prepare a short cover letter summarizing backup encryption and snapshot deletion behavior.

Also flagging that Orbis is asking about multi-region replication — we should only offer that with an explicit buyup (documented second region and added SLA).

Can security prep the deletion report template and one‑sentence answers we can paste into the questionnaire? I’ll send the formal set to Asha once we have those.
